app.title: OpenDose: curve fitting and biostatistics in the browser
app.summary: A person pastes or imports bench measurements into a typed data table (XY, column, grouped, survival and others), or reads a plate-reader export. They can strike out bad values with a reason. They pick a model or test from a searchable library, such as a four-parameter dose-response, and the engine fits it in the browser. It reports best-fit parameters with confidence intervals, fit diagnostics and a drawn curve. The results sheet adds a plain-language results sentence, a figure legend and methods text. The person can copy these, or export the graph and the tables at journal size.

task.text: Fit curves and run standard statistical tests on lab measurements, and get publication-ready numbers, figures and methods text.

data.text: Tables of measured responses entered by hand, pasted from a spreadsheet or imported from instrument exports. Each data set has replicate subcolumns, often responses against concentration.
data.item: a data set (a column of replicate responses) in a project data table, such as one compound's responses across concentrations

stage.text: analysing cleaned bench results and writing them up for a paper

mechanism.text: A navigator lists the project's data tables, each with its results and graphs. Selecting a table opens a workspace where the data grid, the analysis controls, the live graph and the results sheet sit side by side and recompute when the data or options change. Under the results come a results sentence, the figure legend and methods text to copy, and export controls for the graph.

field.text: dose-response curve fitting and biostatistics for wet-lab experiments

workflow.name: fit a model to measurements and report the fitted values

steps.here: Paste from Excel into a typed data table, use the Import dialog (delimiter, decimal comma, column roles), or use the plate importer for SRB/MTT viability plates. A paste report counts the numbers read.
Ctrl/Cmd+E strikes a value out and asks for a reason. Analyses and graphs skip it, and the results list n entered, excluded and analysed. A Data Inspector summarises the selected block.
A searchable, family-grouped equation picker offers models such as log(inhibitor) vs. response with four parameters, along with constraints, weighting, CI method and shared parameters.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The browser-side engine fits the curve and reports Top, Bottom, LogIC50, HillSlope and IC50 with asymptotic or profile CIs, R² and Sy.x. It also flags ambiguous fits and extrapolated IC50s.
A graph draws points with error bars and the fitted curve on a log concentration axis, and redraws whenever the data or the fit change.
Under the results sit a results sentence, the figure legend and methods text, each ready to copy. Copy for Word pastes the results as a formatted table.
Export the graph as PNG, TIFF, SVG or PDF at an exact width, height and DPI, or to PowerPoint. Export the results as CSV or TSV, and save the project as a file.

distinctive: All computation runs in the browser through Pyodide, so the data never leaves the machine.
Every excluded value keeps its reason, and the reasons flow through to the n counts, the legend and the methods text.
The fitted IC50/EC50 comes with asymmetric confidence intervals, and a value beyond the tested range is reported as not reached.
Results, legend and methods text are generated together, so the reported numbers, n and test description stay consistent.
The project navigator keeps each table together with its results and graphs, and linked tables (transform, normalise) stay live.
